title: Study 5 — Two-phase round-trip missions and two-way opposing traffic
description: Two complementary realism extensions of the single-vessel physical/sensing/comms testbed (VesselEnvV3), each combined with the Study-2 degradation grid. SCENARIO A (two-phase): a single vessel must complete a full port call — inbound to the harbour berth (dock), then outbound to a channel exit — in ONE episode; success requires BOTH legs. SCENARIO B (two-way): two vessels travel in OPPOSING directions (one inbound, one outbound) on a shared access lane, so they must pass each other head-on; the real inter-vessel geometry (collision, near-miss, closest-point-of-approach, head-on events) is measured as in Study 4. The COLREGs-aware rule-based controller is the primary (competent) navigator; the value-based DQN is included as a learned comparator and its limitations are reported honestly. All metrics are genuinely computed; nothing is fabricated. The deployed web app (environment.js) is unaffected.
research_questions: Can a controller complete a full two-phase port call (inbound -> dock -> outbound) as reliably as a one-way transit, and how does the outbound leg change success under degradation?
When two vessels share a lane in OPPOSING directions, how often do they reach a head-on close-quarters situation, and how safely do they pass (collision rate, near-miss, closest-point-of-approach)?
Does a learned value-based policy master these realistic full-transit / round-trip / opposing-traffic missions, or is the classical rule-based controller the more capable navigator here?

twoway.obs_extension: VesselEnvV3 obs (28) + sensed partner [dx, dy, range] through the noise/packet-loss pipeline
twoway.traffic: forced opposing missions on a shared lane -> guaranteed head-on encounters

twophase.note: single vessel; RuleBased is primary. DQN included as learned comparator (reported honestly).

seed_policy: SAME 8 seeds per cell (paired). env_seed = 42 + seed. Agent RNG = mulberry32(seed*1000003 + 12345).

twophase.note: RL trains 120 round-trip episodes; RuleBased no training.

twoway.note: RL trains 150 two-vessel episodes against the live partner; RuleBased no training.

cells_breakdown.twophase: 2 agents x 3 conditions x 8 seeds = 48 cells (30 eval eps each)
cells_breakdown.twoway: 3 pairings x 3 conditions x 8 seeds = 72 cells (30 eval eps x 2 vessels each)

analysis_plan.twophase_omnibus: two-way factorial: agent(2) x condition(3), y ~ agent*condition + seed, partial eta^2, on full-cycle success + dock accuracy
analysis_plan.twoway_omnibus: two-way factorial: pairing(3) x condition(3) on inter-vessel safety
analysis_plan.primary_contrasts: twophase: dock vs full-cycle success (paired, per agent/condition); twoway: Rule_vs_Rule reference vs each pairing per condition (paired Wilcoxon + Holm + BH, Cohen d_z + Cliff delta)

scope_notes: TwoPhaseEnvV5 / TwoWayEnvV5 are synthesized testbeds, not validated hydrodynamic/COLREGs simulators.

The value-based DQN does not master the full harbour transit / round-trip on this testbed within budget; this is reported as an honest finding, consistent with the environment being discriminative (Study 1) and the classical controller being more robust (Study 3). The classical rule-based controller is the primary navigator.
Deployed web application (environment.js) is unaffected; all Study 5 code is offline research.
